title: Quarterly Roadmap: Hosted API + Model Catalog — Incremental Rollout & Risk Mitigation Plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: Context: Q2 quarter plan to align hosted API model lineup rotation with deployments, canary windows, and customer-facing SLAs. This ticket consolidates a staged rollout plan for the model catalog updates that balances performance/cost optimizations with quality guardrails and enterprise risk controls. It covers scheduling, canary criteria, rollback triggers, comms, and post-rollout evaluation targets.
outcome_goals: Deliver model lineup rotation for top-10 hosted endpoints without exceeding error budget
Establish 3-phase canary (internal -> limited customers -> general) with measurable quality gates
Reduce median token latency for chat endpoints by >=8% for canary traffic while holding P99 latency within SLO
Provide playbook for automatic fallback to previous model variants with <=5 minutes mean time to restore (MTTR)
acceptance_criteria: Canary traffic routed and isolated by customer cohort in Canary Region A
Canary evaluation dashboard shows pass/fail for quality (BLEU/ROUGE surrogate, hallucination signal), latency, and cost KPIs
Rollback automation validated in staging and exercised once in internal canary
Runbook and customer comms templates approved by Legal and Support
rollout_plan_phases: Phase 0 — Staging validation (2 weeks): extended inference tests, perf loads, quantization verification on dedicated pool
Phase 1 — Internal canary (3 days): 5% of internal traffic, SLO/quality gating, cross-team sign-off
Phase 2 — Partner-limited canary (1 week): opt-in customers (3 customers), manual monitoring and twice-daily syncs
Phase 3 — Gradual ramp (2 weeks): stepwise traffic increases (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) with automated rollback checks
Phase 4 — Post-rollout baseline (4 weeks): regression alerts, model health dashboarding, begin automated pruning for deprecated variants
metrics_and_thresholds: Quality: hallucination signal <= baseline + 2% (measured on evaluation prompt set)
Cost: per-token compute cost change <= +12% unless approved by finance
User-facing complaint volume: <= 2x baseline per 10k requests during canary window
decisions_made: Prioritize rotation for high-throughput completions endpoints first to maximize cost delta visibility
Use model-compatibility layer to automatically fallback to the last stable quantized variant on metric breach
Adopt rolling canary windows by customer cohort (region + tier) to reduce blast radius
Require security review for any model that introduces new external-weights or third-party data (hence security_review_required = true)
open_blockers: Engineering: finalization of autoscaling policy for canary pools (ENG-43119) — blocks Phase 2
Design: revised error UX templates for deprecation notices to end-users — pending (DES-2207)
Legal: confirmation on billing language for partner-limited canary offers — awaiting response
communication_plan: Pre-canary: announce to beta customers + internal slack channel #hosted-api-ops 72h prior
During canary: twice-daily ops sync (engineering + on-call + PM) and live dashboard link
Rollback comms: templated email + in-console banner for affected customers
Post-rollout: 1-week executive summary and dataset of regression prompts for model performance

2025-02-26 — Legal requested revised partner terms for limited canary. PM to coordinate with Growth for customer outreach messaging.

2025-03-01 — Internal canary successfully executed for internal agents; observed 9% median latency improvement and two regressions flagged by hallucination detector. Debugging led to prompt-tokenization fix; fixes pushed to staging (PR #5137).
2025-03-03 — Decision: proceed to partner-limited canary after one full business day of stable metrics and sign-off from Security. Diego to schedule partner onboarding calls.
postmortem_plan: If rollback occurs: 1) capture state snapshot and logs, 2) run regression eval on canary prompt set, 3) perform RCA within 72 hours and publish findings to confluence
If rollout completes: create model health report, propose next rotation candidates, and add deprecated variants to pruning list
notes: This ticket consolidates PM-level orchestration; engineering tickets referenced in dependencies will own infra implementation. Keep ticket updated with exact canary cohort IDs and any escalation timelines.
